rationale: ROUND 2 of the Thunder orphan sweep (round 1 verdict: REVISE, gated by the guidelines seat). Every round-1 objection is dispositioned below, then the original case restated. (1) GUIDELINES (high, gating) objected to the targetless ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING dedup write and named DELETE+INSERT as the documented idiom. Measured: DELETE FROM site_work_items appears at ZERO call sites in the codebase, so that specific remedy is not the platform's practice — but the objection was right in substance, because a SHARED WRITER exists and round 1 walked around it: load_work_item_actions.go insertWorkItem/writeWorkItem carries the targeted ON CONFLICT (site_id, item_key) WHERE ... NOT IN (workItemTerminalStatuses) clause (the lockstep contract with idx_swi_dedup), within-cycle suppression, and the two-strike unresolved labelling — and the workItem struct's own parentItemID comment records a prior council round (bugs_open/091) objecting to exactly this hand-rolled bypass at three other sites. The filing now goes through insertWorkItem in a transaction, recurrenceExpected=false deliberately (a re-observed orphan after two closes IS a strike). (2) EDITQUALITY's missing item — the FTW-042 register entry asserted but not covered by an edit — is now edit 7; it shipped in the same commit as the code (81484df8a), and the dispatch action's sketch (edit 2) now shows the actual wiring rather than 'copied verbatim'. (3) TOOLING_PROVENANCE: the seed now writes a doc_notes row (subject_type 'pipeline', subject_key 'thunder-orphan-scan') carrying the producer/item_key contract, the grace_minutes tuning knob, and the thunder-lifecycle sharing rationale; measured first, answering the seat's open question: doc_notes carried NO pipeline-subject row for thunder-adapter, thunder-reaper or thunder-lifecycle — only 4 landmine rows — so this is the first durable Postgres-side trace for the group. (4) GUARDIAN's workflow-selection concern is answered by code read, not assumption: platform/messaging/processor.go extractGroupInfo (line 1074) reads config.agent_type FIRST, and the scheduler's fireTrigger builds that field from the scheduled_tasks row's target_agent_type column — the cited landmine is about call_agent CHILDREN whose body lacks that field, which scheduler triggers always carry. Live proof on the identical path: thunder-reaper (same topic system.agent.generic.requests, same task-mode dispatch) ran its own agent_definition workflow to COMPLETED at 17:52Z today, verified in orchestration_states. Guardian's output_field question: dispatch step config output_field='thunder_list', reconcile step config list_field='thunder_list' — shown in edit 6's sketch, and the awaited response lands at collected_data.thunder_list.response, the shape verified against today's live reaper run. (5) DEBUG_HISTORIAN: sql_for_agents has no schema_migrations ledger — the numbering check is the directory listing + git log, run and recorded in the seed header (342 carries only this file; a concurrent lane took 343; the doubled 340/341 pairs in that directory are the race the check exists for); and the seed now carries a DO/RAISE verify block INSIDE the transaction before COMMIT (a SELECT-only verify cannot stop a COMMIT), asserting the agent_definition shape, the scheduled_tasks row, and the doc_notes row, so a botched apply fails loudly instead of committing a half-seeded pipeline. ORIGINAL CASE, unchanged: provision_action.go INSERTs thunder_instances only after the vendor box is up, so a crash in that window or a hand-created instance bills at Thunder invisibly to every automated check; the sweep asks Thunder for its own account view every 6h and reconciles, read-and-report only, no remediation authority (decommission needs the very row an orphan lacks). Collision measurements from round 1 stand: item_type 0 rows across 86 types, both names unclaimed. Code is committed (81484df8a + revision ecbb0f362) per the commit-when-coherent rule; inert until both images roll and 342 is applied, image first.

plan.summary: Thunder instances can bill with no thunder_instances row (provision writes the row only after the box is up; hand-created boxes never get one), and every automated check reads only that table. Add a 6-hourly vendor-truth reconcile: a read-only list_instances action on thunder-adapter, a dispatch action that awaits it, and a reconcile action that classifies vendor-vs-DB and files thunder_orphan work items through insertWorkItem — the shared writer with the idx_swi_dedup lockstep clause and anti-churn — for anything billing invisibly. Ghosts are reported, not filed. Read-and-report only. Revision from round 1: shared-door filing (was hand-rolled ON CONFLICT), doc_notes write-back, DO/RAISE in-transaction verify, register entry covered by an edit.

plan.risks: Unchanged from round 1 in kind — read-and-report, so failure modes are false signals, not damage: a provision slower than 30 minutes flags one scan early (grace_minutes is step config); a scan racing a decommission can report a transient ghost (no work item, and the shared concurrency group excludes the reaper); a missing vendor createdAt flags rather than hides (noise, not silence — the right direction for a billing control). NEW in this revision, for reviewers to check: the filing now inherits insertWorkItem's anti-churn, so an orphan item closed twice in 7 days re-files as 'unresolved' and a re-observation within 3 hours of a close is suppressed entirely — for a 6-hourly scan of a billing condition this is acceptable (the Error log line fires every scan regardless, and unresolved items are visible to the RFC_010 revalidation path), but it IS behaviour the hand-rolled version did not have. The work items still have no automated consumer (dispatch is dead fleet-wide) — the disclosed human path is the Error log, the RUNBOOK 1b query, and now the doc_notes pipeline row; the seed's first-run verification requires the first scan's counts be cross-checked against the manual API call the same day, because a 0-findings run must prove it looked.
